item.title: Mazes, Maps, Glyphs and a Space City
item.description:
After the Commodore 64 it’s back to this century. A pile of Python scripts had been building up in my Google Drive, some drawing fractals and some not. I had Claude fetch them, sort out which were older copies of things already in my fractals repo, install the packages they needed, run them and write them up in the README.

Most of them aren’t fractals at all, so the repo’s name is now a bit of a fib. What they share is the seed: give a script the same number and you get the same picture, or leave it out and see what turns up.

item.title: Generative Art with Context Free
item.description: I’ve got a small repo, ContextFree, that I keep coming back to whenever I want the specific kind of fun that comes from writing a handful of lines of code and having something unexpectedly pretty fall out the other end. It’s a collection of Context Free Art scripts — a tiny grammar for describing images as recursive drawing rules — plus a Docker image wrapping the cfdg renderer so I can run them without installing anything locally.
